title: How we run experiments: decide before you look
subtitle: The Parcel & Pine experimentation playbook: pre-registration, power, guardrails, peeking, when to use a holdout or a geo test, and the one-page decision memo.
summary: This is the team standard for running A/B tests, holdouts and geo tests at Parcel & Pine. Every test is pre-registered with one primary metric, guardrails, an MDE and a fixed end date. The primary metric is read once, and every test ends in a one-page decision memo.
key_findings: At 3.4% baseline conversion, detecting a 2% relative lift needs about 1.1M sessions per arm; a 5% lift needs 178k.
Daily peeking with stop-at-significance inflates the false-positive rate from 5% to about 25% over four weeks.
5 of 14 tests from 2025 that looked like clear winners at week 1 were flat or negative by their planned end date.
Plan on 40–60% of a winning test's point estimate when forecasting impact.
